name: Empty Brown Waterskin
summary: In the Barrens, Brine gives an empty waterskin to a shaman initiate.

sections.title: A Lesson in Scarcity
sections.body: Brine gives a shaman initiate an empty leather skin for the opening trial of the Call of Water. The initiate must carry it to the watering hole beneath her dwelling and return with it full. The pool is guarded by local quilboar, who prize its water. In the Barrens, where water is scarce, even a small oasis can sustain life and spark violence.

faq.q: What is the Empty Brown Waterskin used for?
faq.answer: Shaman initiates use the empty waterskin to draw water from the natural pond beneath Brine's hut in the Barrens. Filled, it is needed to prepare elemental sapta.
Brine, a hermit in the southern Barrens, gives the waterskin to shamans undertaking their elemental pilgrimage to commune with the spirits of water.

faq.q: Why are the quilboar defending the water source?
faq.answer: Rain is rare throughout the Barrens, and water is scarce. To the quilboar, even a small watering hole means wealth and survival, so they guard it and attack anyone who draws from it.

faq.q: What happens once the skin is filled?
faq.answer: Dipped into the oasis beneath Brine's hill, the skin becomes a Filled Brown Waterskin. Returning it to Brine lets her test your understanding of nature's balance before she sends you across the world for rarer waters.

angles.text: As a shaman, carrying this waterskin is a rite of passage on the way to your Water Totem. It shows the balance between reverence for the elements and the harsh struggle to survive.
